operator_io_quirks: ratings has 15.5M rows, ratings_users 4.3M, movies 226k: read_schema must rowid-sample (max_rows_per_table) and never copy rows; original_sizes via count(*).
ratings has NO primary key and NO unique column; lists_users PK is composite (user_id, list_id); lists.list_id and movies.movie_id are single-col PKs.

FK cycle: lists.user_id -> lists_users.user_id and lists_users.user_id -> lists.user_id (and lists_users.list_id -> lists.list_id). process_order must break the table cycle deterministically; column-level cycle too.

ratings has a self-FK rating_id -> ratings.rating_id (parent_exists true) and TWO FKs on user_id (ratings_users and lists_users): fks dict keyed by (child_t, child_c) can hold only one — the second is silently dropped; record which wins (pragma order: ratings_users first).

ratings_users.user_id -> lists_users.user_id but lists_users.user_id is NOT unique (distinct 23118 of 80311): FK to non-unique parent; child draws with replacement from parent values, fine, but no uniqueness guarantee.
lists.user_id -> lists_users.user_id likewise non-unique parent; lists.user_id distinct 22925 vs lists_users.user_id distinct 23118 — dangling child values exist in original.

Declared TEXT but text-stored dates: list_update_timestamp_utc / list_creation_timestamp_utc 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; rating_date_utc, list_update_date_utc, list_creation_date_utc 'YYYY-MM-DD'; rating_timestamp_utc 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. All dispatch to String fuzzer (type TEXT), NOT Date — TS will emit random charset strings, not dates.
movies.director_id is TEXT holding integer-ish ids and comma-joined multi-ids ('89, 90'); String fuzzer int-like branch adds i+1/i-1 strings.

lists_users.user_eligible_for_trial / user_has_payment_method declared TEXT but store '0'/'1' (text storage); same columns in ratings/ratings_users are INTEGER. Mixed declared types across tables for same-named columns.
movie_title_language has distinct=1 ('en') — String sampler with one element will mostly return 'en' perturbed/contaminated.

High null rates: ratings.critic 0.965, ratings_users.user_cover_image_url 0.674, lists.list_description 0.655, lists_users.user_cover_image_url 0.6 — but all columns notnull=0, so TS may emit NULLs freely; original_values include NULLs.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes, no views/triggers in DDL; only PKs and FKs. Table names all lowercase, no spaces — but spec still requires double-quoting.
operator_ts_expectations: All date/timestamp columns are TEXT -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length 0-20 plus contamination; almost no value will parse as a date. Queries filtering rating_date_utc BETWEEN '2010-01-01' AND '2011-01-01' will return empty or garbage -> FN risk (implausible values).

Number fuzzer on INTEGER columns: full range [-10^4,10^4] (scale 0) with +-1/+-2 perturbation; movie_id, list_id, user_id, rating_id get small ints, not the 8-digit ids seen in original -> joins on user_id between ratings and lists_users still work (FK consistency) but filters like user_id > 10000000 return nothing -> FN.

rating_score distinct 5 (1-5) but Number fuzzer ignores that: values spread over [-10000,10000] -> queries rating_score = 5 or BETWEEN 1 AND 5 mostly miss -> FN; also no ties/duplicates at the 5-value granularity -> FP on GROUP BY rating_score / COUNT DISTINCT.

user_trialist/user_subscriber/user_eligible_for_trial/user_has_payment_method are 0/1 flags but Number fuzzer emits wide ints -> WHERE user_subscriber = 1 nearly empty -> FN; GROUP BY these flags yields thousands of groups instead of 2 -> FP.
movie_release_year INTEGER (not 'year' type) -> Number fuzzer, not the year branch; values in [-10000,10000] -> WHERE movie_release_year = 2007 misses -> FN.

String fuzzer on list_title, movie_title, director_name: random charset strings, not real titles; LIKE '%love%' queries miss -> FN; but contamination adds %-stripped variants and +-1 int strings, giving some spurious matches -> FP.

list_movie_number, list_followers, list_comments, critic_likes, critic_comments are small-count INTEGERs; Number fuzzer wide range -> ORDER BY / LIMIT / HAVING count > N queries get implausible distributions -> FN and FP.

FK consistency: ratings.user_id drawn from lists_users.user_id (final filtered) and ratings_users.user_id; lists.user_id from lists_users.user_id. But lists_users.user_id itself is drawn from lists.user_id (cycle) — TS draws child before parent in level order, so one direction may see empty parent -> NULLs -> join queries return empty -> FN.
ratings has no PK: sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op, drop_unique_duplicates no-op -> duplicate rows possible; COUNT(*) / DISTINCT queries get inflated or tied counts -> FP on ties.

lists_users composite PK (user_id, list_id): sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate tuples; but user_id and list_id each drawn independently -> many distinct pairs, few natural ties -> FP on GROUP BY user_id HAVING count(*)>1.

Self-FK ratings.rating_id -> ratings.rating_id: child draws from parent's final rating_id column (same table, already generated) — with no PK filter, values are wide ints; self-join queries on rating_id mostly empty -> FN.
String fuzzer on list_url, movie_url, *_image_url: random strings, not URLs; LIKE 'http%' misses -> FN; but original_values (5 sampled) include real URLs so some rows match -> partial.
